title: Launch Runway Buffer & Surge Capacity Manifest for Release Trains (runtime/console/API)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Define a lightweight, repeatable policy and operational artifact (the 'Surge Capacity Manifest') that each release train must publish before cutover. The manifest standardizes runway buffer windows, surge capacity reservations (dedicated pools or burst tokens), routing fallback tiers, and stakeholder RACI so runtime/console/API launches can be executed with predictable latency and minimal cross-team confusion.

Why: Recent cross-surface launches exposed gaps in capacity hedging and ownership during peak traffic. Teams resorted to ad-hoc overprovisioning and pager handoffs. A canonical manifest removes ambiguity and makes the launch calendar actionable for SRE/Infra/Capacity teams while keeping utilization efficient.

Scope: Applies to all coordinated release trains impacting runtime, console, or public API surfaces. The artifact includes: runway window, buffer size (tokens or GPU slots), surge activation criteria (SLO/latency/queue-depth thresholds), fallback routing matrix, canary phasing plan, cutover and rollback signals, and post-cutover observation checklist.

Non-goals: This ticket does not provision capacity automatically or replace dedicated capacity contracts; instead it defines the policy, templates, and ops playbook and coordinates required engineering work for automation in follow-on tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest template exists in Confluence with fields for runway window, buffer size, surge activation criteria, fallback routing tiers, and RACI
Three cross-team launch rehearsals completed using the manifest and measured against predefined SLO gates
Automated checklist populated in the release calendar UI (Console) showing buffer reservations and ownership
Post-launch telemetry dashboard (latency, error-rate, consumption of buffer) created and linked
Roll-forward/rollback signal definitions agreed and documented with SRE and infra
